newsitem.title: USA: FEATURE-Debate rages as TV character reveals she is gay.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE-Debate rages as TV character reveals she is gay.

text.p: U.S. television threw its biggest coming out party ever this week when comedian Ellen DeGeneres's sitcom alter ego, a seemingly asexual bookstore manager named Ellen Morgan, announced "I'm gay."

It was the moment all America had been told to expect -- with or without bated breath -- for months since the story first broke in TV Guide magazine, raising questions as to whether television was striking a blow for tolerance or engaging in yet another attention-grabbing publicity stunt.

For gay groups, who threw their own parties around the country on Wednesday night to celebrate, Ellen Morgan's coming out was a moment of long-awaited boldness -- the first time a central character on a comedy show had been revealed as openly gay. DeGeneres's four-year-old show "Ellen," which has been struggling to stay on the air, was expected to attract up to 20 million viewers and critics called it, sight unseen, a highlight of the season.

Some of the biggest stars of the small screen put in cameo appearances to give their stamp of approval on the one-hour special, which just happened to coincide with sweeps week -- the ratings of programs' relative popularity on which advertising rates are based. They included Laura Dern, who plays the woman Ellen falls for and who has already given interviews saying she is hopelessy hetereosexual, Demi Moore, k.d. lang, Billy Bob Thornton and -- STOP THE PRESSES -- Oprah Winfrey, the talk show host who is a symbol of middle-American sensibility.
Winfrey plays Ellen's therapist and the message is that if it is OK for Oprah, it should be OK for America.
ANOTHER BATTLEGROUND IN U.S. CULTURE WARS

But many conservative groups are complaining that it is not OK and the show has become yet another battleground in the country's culture wars -- even though far more sensational things happen in films and in books than on television.

As Time Magazine noted, one of the season's bestsellers is a woman's account of her willing affair with her father and one of the year's biggest films celebrates a drug-addicted pornographer, holding him up as an icon of free speech.

Carman Pate, vice president of the 500,000-member Concerned Women for America, said her group strongly opposed the show because, "even though it has no violence or partial nudity it has a message that can strongly impact a child for life. ... It glorifies a lifestyle that is dangerous. This is not a civil rights issue. Homosexuality can be changed."

But Peg Byron, public education director of the Lambda Legal Defence Fund, one of the nation's oldest gay groups, said all the programme did was narrow the gap between television and the real world -- a world where gay people exist, work and lead normal, productive lives. "Stereotypes are harmful and 'Ellen' undermines America's denials about lesbianism."
SURPRISE LOST WHEN WORD LEAKED OUT

DeGeneres originally wanted the show to be a surprise and when word leaked out she found herself at first dissembling, pretending that her character was going to reveal that she was "Lebanese" -- not lesbian.

But in the last few weeks she has beat her character to the punch, announcing in magazine and TV interviews that she, herself, is gay, something she had kept private until now. She and her girl friend, actress Anne Heche, have been making public appearances including at last week's White House Correspondents Dinner, where they were photographed with President Bill Clinton.

Daniel Cerone, the TV Guide reporter who broke the story, says the programme caused a stir with advertisers. Some, like Chrysler, dropped plans to advertise on it, but others rushed in and are paying ABC premium rates because of the huge ratings the show was expected to receive.

"'Ellen' was a series on the border. Its rating are in the middle of the pack but it didn't have a focus. I don't think having her character come out is an attempt for ratings as much as making the show represent Ellen DeGeneres's point of view," Cerone said.
The real problems for the show are yet to come -- whether it will be renewed for next season and, if it is, how it will deal with its main character's homosexuality, he added.
